claims.statement: Every `/app/v1/*` route registers onto the single aiohttp application that `build_health_app` already builds, rather than a second app, so the portal API shares one port with `/health` and `/metrics` — `[obs.metrics].port`, which `config.example.toml` annotates as also serving `/health`.

`register_web_routes` takes every collaborator as a keyword and stores it under a `web_*` key on the application, and the sibling registrations `register_document_history_routes` and `register_artifact_routes` read those keys — which is why they are called at the end of `register_web_routes` and would raise `KeyError` if called first.

No `/app/v1` read authenticates its caller: the reads trust the private docker network and the portal proxy in front of them. The one-time-code pair is the single exception, because it hands out a `personId` — it requires a bearer token named by `[otp] api_token_env`, compared in constant time, is mounted only when `[otp] enabled`, and `register_otp_routes` refuses to register with an empty token.

The portal's session and allowlist logic lives in one function, `checkSession()`, which re-reads the same `identity.toml` bytes Nora's process reads (cached, re-read on mtime change) and resolves both Discord sign-in and one-time-code sign-in to one identity.toml person, so somebody removed from the roster is refused on their next request whichever way they signed in.

The portal reaches Nora's API through one table, `ROUTES` in `app/src/server/upstream.ts`, which enforces GET only, forwards only the query parameters a route names, overwrites `personId` from the session on `scope: "self"` routes (ignoring a browser-supplied value), re-encodes id-shaped path parameters, and prefers literal segments over parameters so `presence/analytics/places` cannot be read as a person named `analytics`.

The three derived-presence endpoints are wrapped in `_needs_a_build`, which turns `NoRollupBuildError` into a 503 `{"error": "unavailable", "reason": "no Rollup build yet"}` instead of an empty 200 — because with no build yet, 'no places, no rhythm, no routes' would be a false statement about data that was never derived.

The games routes proxy Pulse's REST API and convert every `GamesUnavailableError` into one fixed generic 503 body (`{"error": "games backend unavailable"}`), logging the real exception server-side so tailnet hostnames, MCP payloads and Pulse's own error text never reach a browser.

Documents, artifacts, events and the evidence text inside a memory entry are gated by `rooms_of(person_id)`, a callable so `nora.web` never imports a `Policy`; composition binds it as `functools.partial(rooms_named, allowlist)` where `allowlist` is the single `Policy` `load_policy` returned while `build_dependencies` ran, so the room set is recomputed on every request (nothing is cached between reads) but `policy.toml` is never re-read — a room-membership edit on disk takes effect only when the process is recreated, the same load-once lifetime `identity.toml` and `policy.toml` share.

A document or artifact the viewer may not see, a deleted one, a picture the document does not name, and one that never existed all answer the same 404; no portal route returns a distinct 'forbidden', because a ref must never confirm that a thing exists.

Live and historical presence are not room-scoped and deliberately bypass `DisclosureGuard`: every allowlisted portal viewer sees every `identity.toml` circle member, a stated product decision; `presence=None` (feature off or no circle) yields an empty list or 404 rather than an error, and a non-circle `person_id` on the history route is `None`/404 while a real but empty history is a 200 with `points: []`.

The presence analytics routes resolve their subject against the same circle roster the presence route renders (`_analytics_subject_ids`), so an unknown or non-member `subjectId` gets an empty shape and the mobility store is never read — the endpoint is not an existence oracle.

`/app/v1/memory` is self-scoped: a missing or unrecognized `personId` answers `[]` rather than any other person's data (fail closed), and each entry is one per Nora workspace that names the caller, keeping Honcho's identity claims (`peer_card`) and its dated episodes (`representation`, observer = the AI peer) as two separate lists rather than one merged list.

`/app/v1/status` is a filtered re-projection of what `/health` computes plus a reminders summary: it names reminders by due time, platform and conversation only (never their text or requester), and it omits any cross-room 'recent activity' field because `RecordStore.recent()` is scoped to one conversation and no port method spans rooms.

The process start time is created once in `App.run` and handed to both `build_health_app` and `register_web_routes`, so `/health`'s uptime and `/app/v1/status`'s `uptime_seconds` cannot disagree about when the process started.

`POST /app/v1/documents/{id}/state` is the portal's state write and reuses the read gate (`DocumentStore.get_visible`): whoever may open a document may archive, delete or restore it, a document they may not open or a deleted one is the same 404, and a store exception is answered `unavailable` (503) rather than 'not found'.

A document revision restore republishes an old spec as a new revision through the store's compare-and-swap (`base_revision`), records `portal:<person_id>` as the writer, and answers 409 for a stale `base_revision`, an archived document or an invalid spec — history is never rewritten.

Document pictures and artifact downloads are typed again from the bytes rather than from the stored row, and are served with `nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` and `private, no-store`; only a raster picture may display inline for a document, while artifacts additionally allow audio and video inline and mark everything else an attachment.

`/app/v1/events(/{id})` require a valid `personId`, and a room-only event is listed only when the policy-bound `room_event_shown` collaborator admits the viewer; without that callable no room-only event is listed at all (fail closed), and an event the viewer neither created, answered nor shares a room with is the same 404 as an unknown id.

Route handlers in `nora/web/api.py` stay thin — query parsing and validation, viewer resolution, and mapping a payload builder's result to an HTTP status — while the payload construction and the visibility gates live in per-area modules (`nora/web/documents.py`, `artifacts.py`, `memory.py`, `presence.py`, `gatherings.py`) that take typed collaborators rather than the application object.

`rooms_named` returns every id form (`id` plus `also_ids`) of each room whose `persons` names the person, and leaves out a `persons = "*"` room entirely because such a room names nobody — so only a document's creator reads what was made there — while the creator clause itself is unconditional and reaches the database as the single predicate `created_by = person_id` OR the document's `(platform, conversation_id)` among the viewer's rooms, the same predicate the listing, the detail and a search all apply in the statement that reads.

A room's label is shown only to a viewer whose own rooms include that room: a creator who has since left the room still reads the document, its detail and its revision history, but every payload gives them `roomLabel: ""` and no chat id, so the label of a room a person is not in is never theirs to see.

The web tests named for revocation prove next-read evaluation, not live membership changes: `test_removing_a_person_from_a_room_revokes_access_on_the_next_read` and `test_leaving_the_room_revokes_on_the_next_request` reassign the test world's `Policy` object and re-request, and the documents test's own comment records that the object is loaded at startup so in production a removal takes effect at the next restart.
